## Title

`feat(gui): introduce an ASCII cellular-automaton design programme and apply it to every screen`

## Summary

Introduces a minimalistic ASCII / cellular-automaton design programme for the game GUI, packaged as a set of design modules under `src/gui/design/` and as the `gui-design-program` skill. Every screen and overlay is restyled from the programme's tokens and classes, so the interface is now built from characters on a grid — void ground, one monospace family, one accent, hairline rules, and dividers generated by an elementary automaton.

## Motivation

The GUI had no design language. Each screen carried its own hand-written `style.cssText` string, so colours (`#111`, `#fff`, `rgba(0,0,0,0.6)`), font sizes, and spacings were repeated and drifted between screens, buttons had no hover, focus, or disabled treatment, and there was nothing to consult before writing the next screen. The interface also looked nothing like the thing it simulates.

## Changes

### Files Deleted

- None

### Files Updated

- **`src/gui/design/DesignTokens.ts`** (new) — `DESIGN_TOKENS`: every colour, font size, tracking, spacing step, fixed measure, border width, and the ornament automaton's rule number, generation count, and column count.
- **`src/gui/design/DesignClasses.ts`** (new) — `DESIGN_CLASS`: the complete set of class names screens are allowed to use, so markup and stylesheet cannot drift.
- **`src/gui/design/DesignStyleSheet.ts`** (new) — `buildDesignStyleSheet()` emits the tokens as `:root` custom properties and defines one rule per `DESIGN_CLASS` entry, including `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, and `:disabled` states; `installDesignStyleSheet()` injects it once, keyed by the `automata-design` element id.
- **`src/gui/design/ElementaryAutomaton.ts`** (new) — `generateAutomatonRows(columns, generations, ruleNumber)`: pure, toroidal, single-live-cell-seeded elementary automaton rendered as `#`/`.` rows; validates all three arguments with `RangeError`.
- **`src/gui/design/AsciiOrnament.ts`** (new) — `createAsciiDivider()` (Rule 90 row after 16 generations), `formatBracketed()` (`[ TITLE ]`), `formatPrompted()` (`> HEADING`).
- **`src/gui/design/index.ts`** (new) — barrel for the design modules.
- **`src/gui/index.ts`** — re-exports the design barrel alongside the existing GUI exports.
- **`src/gui/GameController.ts`** — calls `installDesignStyleSheet()` in the constructor, before any screen is built; class JSDoc notes the added responsibility.
- **`src/gui/screens/TitleScreen.ts`** — title is `[ AUTOMATA ]`, heading is `> HI-SCORE`, an automaton divider sits above and below the list, and the new private `formatEntry()` pads rank/name/score into aligned columns on the character grid; all `style.cssText` replaced by `DESIGN_CLASS`.
- **`src/gui/screens/GameConfigurationScreen.ts`** — title `[ CONFIGURE ]`, headings `> GAME MODE`, `> LEVEL`, `> SELECT 3 RULES`, rule checkboxes drawn as `[ ]`/`[X]` via `DESIGN_CLASS.CHECK`, selects and buttons restyled; the custom-level, custom-mode, and positioning blocks keep their `style.display` show/hide toggle but take their layout from `DESIGN_CLASS.STACK`.
- **`src/gui/screens/GameOverScreen.ts`** — title `[ GAME OVER ]` with a divider, using the veil screen variant so the final grid stays visible behind it.
- **`src/gui/screens/ScoreBoardOverlay.ts`** — uses the shared top overlay bar and row classes; the participant colour remains inline, as it is data rather than styling.
- **`src/gui/screens/SpeedControlOverlay.ts`** — uses the shared bottom overlay bar, the shared button class (which now supplies the disabled treatment at the ends of the speed range), and a fixed-width readout class in place of its local button style constant.
- **`index.html`** — adds a four-line `<style>` setting the void ground, so the page does not flash white before the stylesheet is installed.
- **`.claude/skills/gui-design-program/SKILL.md`** (new) — the design programme as a skill: seven laws, the token/class map, a screen-building recipe, a rendered specimen, an explicit prohibited list, and a review checklist.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — adds `gui-design-program` to the project skill table, to be loaded before any development on `src/gui/`.
- **`tests/gui/design/ElementaryAutomaton.test.ts`** (new) — 9 cases covering row shape, seeding, the Rule 90 Sierpinski expansion, edge wrapping, the rendered characters, an alternative rule, and all three validation failures.
- **`tests/gui/design/DesignStyleSheet.test.ts`** (new) — 3 cases asserting that the tokens reach the stylesheet as custom properties, that every `DESIGN_CLASS` value has a rule, and that the checkbox is drawn as `[ ]`/`[X]`.
- **`tests/gui/design/AsciiOrnament.test.ts`** (new) — 4 cases covering both ASCII formatters, including an empty label.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Establish the design vocabulary

**Pre-condition**: GUI styling exists only as per-element `style.cssText` strings inside each screen.

1. Add `src/gui/design/DesignTokens.ts` exporting `DESIGN_TOKENS` with `COLOR`, `FONT`, `SPACE`, `MEASURE`, `BORDER_WIDTH`, and `ORNAMENT` groups, so every visual value has exactly one home.
2. Add `src/gui/design/DesignClasses.ts` exporting `DESIGN_CLASS`, naming each class the programme defines, so screens never write a literal class string.
3. Add `src/gui/design/ElementaryAutomaton.ts` exporting `generateAutomatonRows(columns, generations, ruleNumber)`, seeding one live cell, wrapping at both edges like the game's toroidal grid, and throwing `RangeError` on invalid width, generation count, or rule number — the ornament must come from a real automaton, not a decorative graphic.

**Post-condition**: The vocabulary of the programme exists as pure, importable modules with no DOM dependency.

### Phase 2 — Build the stylesheet and the ornament

**Pre-condition**: Phase 1 complete; `DESIGN_TOKENS`, `DESIGN_CLASS`, and `generateAutomatonRows` are available.

1. Add `src/gui/design/DesignStyleSheet.ts` with `buildDesignStyleSheet()`, emitting the tokens as `:root` custom properties and one CSS rule per `DESIGN_CLASS` value — including `.ca-check::before { content: '[ ]' }` / `:checked::before { content: '[X]' }`, and the button hover/focus/disabled states screens previously lacked.
2. In the same file add `installDesignStyleSheet()`, injecting a `<style id="automata-design">` only when that id is absent, so rebuilding the controller cannot stack stylesheets.
3. Add `src/gui/design/AsciiOrnament.ts` with `createAsciiDivider()` — the last row of `DESIGN_TOKENS.ORNAMENT.GENERATIONS` generations of Rule 90 — plus `formatBracketed()` and `formatPrompted()` for titles and headings.
4. Add `src/gui/design/index.ts` and re-export it from `src/gui/index.ts`, matching how `screens/` is exposed.

**Post-condition**: A single call installs the whole programme, and screens have factories for every ASCII element they need. Depends on Phase 1.

### Phase 3 — Apply the programme to every screen

**Pre-condition**: Phase 2 complete; the stylesheet and ornament helpers exist.

1. Call `installDesignStyleSheet()` from the `GameController` constructor, before the screens are constructed, so a screen never renders before its classes are defined.
2. Replace every `style.cssText` assignment in `TitleScreen.ts`, `GameConfigurationScreen.ts`, `GameOverScreen.ts`, `ScoreBoardOverlay.ts`, and `SpeedControlOverlay.ts` with a `DESIGN_CLASS` assignment; keep `style.display` toggles and the participant swatch colour, which are behaviour and data rather than styling.
3. Rewrite the screen copy in the programme's idiom: `formatBracketed` for the one title per screen, `formatPrompted` for section headings, `createAsciiDivider()` between blocks, and `TitleScreen.formatEntry()` to align hi-score columns by string padding.
4. Add the void ground to `index.html` so the first paint is black.

**Post-condition**: No GUI file contains a colour, size, spacing, or font value; `grep -rn "cssText" src/gui/` returns nothing. Depends on Phase 2.

### Phase 4 — Package the programme as a skill and cover it with tests

**Pre-condition**: Phase 3 complete; the applied programme is the reference implementation.

1. Add `.claude/skills/gui-design-program/SKILL.md` stating the seven laws, the file map, the screen-building recipe, a rendered specimen, the prohibited list, and the per-file checklist.
2. Add the skill to the project skill table in `CLAUDE.md`, triggered by any development on `src/gui/`.
3. Add `tests/gui/design/` covering the automaton, the stylesheet builder, and the ASCII formatters — the three pure parts of the programme.

**Post-condition**: The programme is loadable as a skill before any future GUI work, and its pure logic is regression-covered. Depends on Phase 3.

## Testing

### TypeScript unit tests

Added:

- `tests/gui/design/ElementaryAutomaton.test.ts` — row count and width, centre seeding, Rule 90 producing the Sierpinski triangle, toroidal wrapping, the exported live/dead characters, an alternative rule number, and the three `RangeError` guards.
- `tests/gui/design/DesignStyleSheet.test.ts` — tokens present as custom property values, a rule present for every `DESIGN_CLASS` value (so a class added without a rule fails the build), and the ASCII checkbox content.
- `tests/gui/design/AsciiOrnament.test.ts` — `formatBracketed` and `formatPrompted`, including an empty label.

No tests were added for the DOM-producing code (`createAsciiDivider`, `installDesignStyleSheet`, the screens): the Vitest environment is `node` and the project has no DOM implementation installed, so those paths are covered by the manual validation steps below.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] All tests passing (`npm run test`)

Not yet executed — no browser was driven in this change. Run `npm run dev` and check:

| # | Check | How to verify |
|---|-------|---------------|
| 1 | Programme installed once | Open dev tools; exactly one `<style id="automata-design">` in `<head>`, and the page ground is black from first paint |
| 2 | Title screen | Shows `[ AUTOMATA ]`, an automaton divider above and below `> HI-SCORE`, and aligned rank/name/score columns |
| 3 | Button states | The "Play game" button turns accent-red on hover and on keyboard focus; the config screen's "Start game" button is faint and non-interactive until three rules are selected |
| 4 | ASCII checkboxes | Rule rows read `[ ]` unselected and accent-red `[X]` selected; the unselected rows go faint once three are chosen |
| 5 | Custom controls still toggle | Choosing "Custom" for level and for game mode reveals the extra selects; choosing a preset hides them again |
| 6 | Overlays | Scoreboard sits top-centre and the speed bar bottom-centre, both bordered on a translucent ground; the speed readout does not reflow as the level changes; the slow/fast buttons show the disabled treatment at the ends of the range |
| 7 | Game over | `[ GAME OVER ]` with a divider over a veil that leaves the final grid visible |

## Additional Notes

- The ornament is Rule 90 taken after 16 generations at 47 columns, which lands on a dense `#.#.#…` band; changing `DESIGN_TOKENS.ORNAMENT` changes every divider in the game at once.
- The accent is the human player's red brightened to `#ff4136` for legibility on black. Player colours themselves are untouched, so the simulation's own palette and the scoreboard swatches still match exactly.
- Selection and focus are always carried by a character (`[X]`, `>`, `[ ]`) as well as by colour, so no state is signalled by colour alone.
- Screen visibility toggles still use `style.display`, which is behaviour rather than styling; this is called out as the explicit exception in the skill's prohibited list.
